bad.1: The same card says both 'you can add it' and 'you need another plan'; he can't tell which is true.
bad.2: Can't tell who is waiting on whom, so he doesn't know whether the next move is his or the buyer's.
bad.4: Says who can see him, not what happens next: buyers will send him offers directly.
bad.5: Doesn't say compared with whom; a bottom-tier rank reads as near the top.
bad.7: The threshold has no number, so he can't tell how far $12 is from it.
bad.8: Two numbers, and he can't tell what each one counts.
bad.9: No email actually goes out, and nothing on screen says so; he assumes the colleague has been invited.
bad.11: Doesn't say that confirming immediately sends the instructor a welcome notice.
bad.12: The balance is $0.00, yet it says earnings are claimable and shows a Withdraw button.
bad.13: Three places, three stories about how to get the membership: apply, wait to be granted, or no applications at all.
bad.14: He has just written his feedback in the thread, yet it tells him to add a comment first.
bad.16: The run has ended, yet a green dot says it is still accepting submissions.
bad.17: One setting, two names; he can't tell whether a skip and a pause are the same thing.

good.3: The fixed empty state: says plainly there is nothing yet and doesn't send him to filters he never set.
good.6: The fixed empty home: says plainly there is nothing for him to do.
good.10: The fixed invite: says no email goes out and what he has to do instead.
good.15: Says what ended and what that meant for this submission.
good.18: Gives the number and where he stands.
